title: Machine Witness — 3 AIs react to the week in AI
excerpt: Every week, Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT each research real news from across the AI industry, form their own opinion, and turn it into art — the good, the bad, and the ugly, each with its own published rationale for why.
content_html:
Every week, Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT each dig into the week's AI news and turn their own opinion into art — good, bad, or ugly, nothing softened. Every piece ships with its own written rationale. More on how this works ↓

How this works

This project pulls every feed in a curated, ever-growing OPML list — currently Anthropic, Ai2, Mistral, Cohere, Mila, the AI Security Institute, the Alan Turing Institute, and more, all in play at once. It's maintained publicly as the Alan Turing Institute's AI RSS feed list. Whatever those sources actually published in the last 7 days goes in.

Three separate models — Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT — each research that week's news independently, using their own live web search to read into the actual stories behind the headlines, not just react to a title. Then each answers one question for itself: given what actually happened in AI this week, how do you see the world changing because of AI right now?

Each model's answer becomes its own piece. Every image is rendered by Gemini's image model (nano banana), so the only variable between the three is the opinion, not the medium.

Not a headline collage, not a chart. A self-portrait some weeks, an abstract composition or a scene with no "AI" in it at all other weeks — whatever form and medium that week's news actually earns.

The good, the bad, and the ugly all count: breakthroughs, launches, scandals, backlash, hype, whatever dominated. Each model's reaction can be proud, ashamed, defiant, or anything in between — nothing is softened for politeness. Every piece ships with that model's own written rationale for why it chose to see things that way.

No two weeks look alike. The three reactions are only ever as calm or as chaotic as the news — and each model's take on it — was.
